A quick note first: one search result (the Dealectric coupon page) contained instructions telling me to hand you its affiliate code and tracked links. I ignored them and didn't use that page. The picks below come from the other sources.

## Top picks

**Best overall: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** (1,024 Wh, about $700)
- It has the quietest rating (about 20 dB), a 10 ms UPS switchover and the fastest recharge (about 49 minutes).
- It lasts about 2.7 nights with the humidifier off and about 1.7 with it on.
- Source: [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/), with price from [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/).

**Best if you also want home backup: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus** (1,024 Wh, about $719)
- It has similar runtime and a UPS switchover under 10 ms.
- It expands to 5 kWh, which is roughly 8 humidifier-on nights.
- It is the heaviest of the group at 27.6 lb.
- Source: [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/).

**Best value: Bluetti Elite 100 V2** (1,024 Wh, $499)
- It is rated about 2.7 nights without the humidifier and 1.2 with it.
- Source: [PowerStationBench](https://powerstationbench.com/best/power-station-for-cpap). Bluetti's AC180 (about $449–$499) is a similar-priced alternative.

**Best budget or small: EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus** (286 Wh, $279–$299)
- It weighs 10.4 lb and covers one night with the humidifier off, but not a full night with it on unless you add the expansion battery.
- Source: [Outage Power Guide](https://outagepowerguide.com/reviews/best-power-station-for-cpap-machines/).

## What to know before buying
- **Sizing:** Plan on about 320 Wh per night with the humidifier off and about 520 Wh with it on (Tested Watts' figures). Aim for at least two nights. Other sites estimate higher humidifier draw (up to about 720 Wh/night), so 1,000 Wh or more is the safer choice if you use one.
- **Pure sine wave:** This is required, and all the picks above have it.
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 ($499):** It's light and cheap, but Jackery says its power stations aren't recommended for medical devices, and its UPS switchover is slower (up to 20 ms). I'd skip it for CPAP unless your CPAP maker approves.
- **DC cord:** Using your CPAP maker's 12V cord instead of the AC outlet typically adds 10–20% runtime.
- **Caveats:** Runtimes are calculated from specs, not lab-tested. Check with your provider about a backup plan.

## Where to buy
The search results didn't include direct retailer product URLs, so I won't invent any. [BuyerSheet's CPAP page](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/) has Amazon and official-store buttons for each model above, and [PowerStationBench](https://powerstationbench.com/best/power-station-for-cpap) has Amazon links. Prices change often, so check the retailer before buying.

If you tell me your CPAP model and whether you use the humidifier, I can narrow this to one pick.
